Off: one list for every network

When the phone moves to a cellular network the tunnel moves onto a server from this list and stays within it: a replacement for a failure is taken from here too. While the list is empty nothing changes and every network shares one list. What counts is the cellular network itself, not a metered one — a temporarily unmetered 5G plan and a home Wi-Fi marked as limited both stay out of it. Put two or three servers here at least; from one there is nowhere to go.
Coming back to Wi-Fi puts the tunnel on the server it left, instead of choosing again

While the tunnel is up, the app probes the current server every 20 seconds. If it fails to answer twice in a row, the servers chosen here are measured afresh: the ones that do not answer drop out, so do the ones that are slow next to the rest, and one of the survivors is picked at random. At random rather than fastest, so that a popular server going down does not send everybody to the same replacement. At most %1$d servers take part, the current one included.
